title: Learning to Split for Automatic Bias Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Applying the Learning to Split (ls) algorithm to the CelebA dataset to identify non-generalizable splits, revealing a spurious correlation between the target attribute (blond hair) and gender (male/female).

Using the Learning to Split (ls) algorithm on the Waterbirds dataset to partition the data and identify generalization gaps caused by the spurious correlation between bird types and their image backgrounds (water vs. land).

Applying the Learning to Split (ls) algorithm on the MNLI dataset to detect generalization failures stemming from spurious shortcuts, specifically the correlation between negation words and contradiction labels.

Using the Learning to Split (ls) algorithm on the Beer Reviews dataset to find non-generalizable data splits caused by strong, spurious correlations between different sentiment aspect ratings (e.g., look vs. aroma).
